advice: Proposal: from `existing-sme` (SHA-256 `3719c58530161598ab9a537a43be749a5287c8d8dbd35b855e5afea97cd15258`), replace the single `n*n` transpose buffer with two `n*VL` FP32 scratch panels allocated inside `gemm`. For each 32-row output panel, transpose that A panel into K-major form, then compute all column tiles for those rows before reusing the panel for the next rows. Keep four ZA accumulators, FP32 MOPAs in increasing-k order, the general GEMM ABI, and current tail predicates. This reduces transpose scratch from 1 MiB to 128 KiB at n=512 and may reduce allocation and scratch initialization/cache traffic. It also changes loop order and panel reuse, so any speed effect must be measured; no gain is established.
risks: The smaller buffer may reduce scratch footprint, but repeated panel preparation or the changed traversal may increase total work or hurt locality. At n=512, two panels total 128 KiB, equal to the supplied P-core L1D capacity, leaving no capacity margin. Preserve allocation failure fallback, n<=0 behavior, arbitrary sizes and odd tails, output overwrite semantics, and reentrancy. Check allocation-size arithmetic, guard regions, and correctness within tolerance 0.002 for small, odd, and full-size cases. Inspect the generated hot-loop assembly for spills and unexpected extra work. Measure full GEMM including packing against unchanged fresh paired AC controls; do not infer a gain from instruction counts or historical scores.
